The Red Door Fits

Elias noted the cabin near the northern ridge at dawn, its red door peeling like a deep sunburn against the grey mist.

By noon, he found the same structure three miles south, identical down to the jagged crack in the upper window, and he whispered, 'It fits just right.'

The map insisted this was impossible, yet when he reached the valley floor, the red door was waiting there again, humming with a soft, copper heat.

He stepped inside to find no floor, only his own silhouette carved into the frame, and as the wood pressed against his spine, he knew it fit just right.
